objective: Test whether the 17 CPVS residuals with both mean magnitudes and missing one band-specific period can be interpolated by a bounded, source-informed multiband Gaussian Process diagnostic.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The 11,602 residuals remain unexplained; no production selector change is authorized.
The shared-period phase-fold diagnostic run 43535760220 found that the 17-object subgroup has median coverage of 92/160 g bins and 91/160 r bins.
The 17 objects retain a positive common Table 2 period, both positive mean magnitudes and raw photometry in both bands.
The matched-control design uses one same-Type Table 4 member per residual, matched on common period, g/r magnitudes and Ng/Nr.

Chan et al. (2022), Section 2.1, specifies george MGPR, normalized phase/wavelength coordinates, separable RBF kernel, constant amplitude, diagonal white noise, zero mean, L-BFGS-B, three phase cycles and a 160-point output grid.

baseline.cohort: 17 candidate-only residuals with both mean magnitudes and one missing band-specific period; 17 deterministic matched Table 4 controls

change.proposed: Add a read-only, bounded MGPR feasibility diagnostic using george==0.4.4.
change.scope: Research-only script, tests and GitHub Actions workflow; no product dependencies, model, selector, feature schema, scientific threshold or baseline artifact changes.
change.rationale: The paper phase-folds both bands using the common Table 2 period. The 17 residuals have adequate observed phase coverage, so MGPR feasibility is the next discriminating experiment.

expected_improvement: Measure optimizer convergence and negative log likelihood for each residual and matched control.
Record fitted phase/wavelength length scales, kernel amplitude, diagonal white-noise variance and covariance condition number.
Generate 160-point posterior mean and uncertainty curves for each band.
Separate a successful numerical fit from scientific membership evidence.

reliability.before: Dependency Audit failed for CVE-2026-114613 in msgpack==1.2.2.
reliability.after: Pending fresh CI; msgpack==1.2.3 is pinned on the PR branch.

correctness.before: Phase coverage was measured, but MGPR feasibility, optimizer behavior and covariance conditioning were unknown.
correctness.evidence: Workflow .github/workflows/cpvs-mgpr-feasibility.yml; script scripts/diagnose_cpvs_mgpr.py; Chan et al. 2022 Section 2.1.

reproducibility.before: The article's MGPR method was known at the equation and procedure level; no project implementation or deterministic test existed.
reproducibility.after: A pinned george==0.4.4 environment, deterministic multi-start settings, input hashes and object-level evidence outputs are defined; CI pending.
reproducibility.evidence: PyPI george 0.4.4; workflow and report schema.

evidence: The paper describes zero mean, a separable RBF phase/wavelength kernel, constant amplitude and diagonal white noise.
The paper specifies L-BFGS-B, repeated phases from 0 to 3 and prediction on phases 2 to 3 with 160 points per band.
The paper does not publish exact optimizer bounds, initial values, george version, or complete implementation.
The diagnostic uses explicit deterministic analyst-selected starts and bounds and labels them as implementation choices.
All raw numeric-valid rows are used; no mapping from Zenodo g_flag/r_flag to DR2 catflags is assumed.
validation.blocker: Run the bounded MGPR workflow, inspect all object-level outputs and verify the report hashes.

root_causes: The 17-object missing-band-period subgroup has adequate shared-period phase coverage; MGPR feasibility remains unmeasured.
limitations: The diagnostic is not an exact reproduction of the authors' unpublished code.
A converged MGPR fit does not prove historical CPVS membership or explain all 11,602 residuals.
Raw Zenodo flag fields have not been proven equivalent to DR2 catflags.

findings: Chan et al. uses the common Table 2 period for both bands, not the per-band Per-g and Per-r values, when phase-folding.
A missing per-band fitted period does not by itself prevent the published common-period MGPR preprocessing.
The paper's MGPR equations and processing sequence can be translated into a bounded diagnostic, but unpublished numerical settings remain explicit uncertainty.

open_blockers: MGPR input preparation tests must pass.
The bounded workflow must complete with finite, traceable outputs or explicit per-object failures.
No production membership rule may be inferred from numerical convergence alone.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not use MGPR convergence as a CPVS membership selector.
Do not change production code or v0.2.0 baseline.
Continue reconstructing the original Chen pipeline, flag semantics and full-parent object-level membership.
